mcqs.question: The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026, passed by Parliament, primarily seeks to achieve which of the following?
options: Decriminalisation of minor offences and promotion of trust-based governance
Abolition of all monetary and civil penalties for regulatory violations
Transfer of all regulatory disputes to criminal courts
Replacement of administrative adjudication with presidential review
mcqs.explanation: The Bill decriminalises minor offences and promotes trust-based governance and ease of doing business. It does not abolish penalties; it converts certain criminal penalties into civil or monetary penalties.

mcqs.question: With reference to the key provisions of the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026, which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Imprisonment for minor offences may be replaced by monetary or civil penalties.
Warnings and improvement notices may precede penalties for initial contraventions.
Enforcement is shifted from criminal courts to administrative adjudication by designated officers and appellate authorities.
Fines are increased by 10% every five years through periodic revision.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that fines are increased by 10% every five years; the prescribed periodic revision is a 10% increase every three years. The other statements correctly describe civil penalties, graded compliance and administrative adjudication.

mcqs.question: In the reported merger of seven of the ten AAP Rajya Sabha MPs with the BJP, the claimed protection under the Tenth Schedule was based on which requirement?
options: A merger supported by two-thirds of the members of the legislature party
A merger supported by one-third of the members of the legislature party
Approval by the President of India
Certification by the Election Commission of India
mcqs.explanation: The MPs claimed protection because the Tenth Schedule permits a merger supported by two-thirds of the legislature party. The earlier one-third split provision was removed by the 91st Amendment, 2003.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Disqualification under the anti-defection law is decided by the President or the Election Commission of India.
Statement B: In Kihoto Hollohan v Zachillhu, the Speaker’s decision was held to be subject to judicial review.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is false because disqualification is decided by the Speaker or Chairman, not the President or Election Commission. Statement B is true because Kihoto Hollohan v Zachillhu held that the Speaker’s decision is subject to judicial review.

mcqs.keyword: First nominated member in the office
mcqs.question: Harivansh’s re-election as Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha was notable for which distinction?
options: He became the first nominated member to become Deputy Chairman
He became the first member elected by secret ballot to become Deputy Chairman
He became the first Deputy Chairman elected under the Tenth Schedule
He became the first Deputy Chairman elected by the President
mcqs.explanation: Harivansh became the first nominated member to become Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. He was nominated by President Droupadi Murmu and was elected through a voice vote under the applicable Rajya Sabha procedure.

mcqs.keyword: First BJP Chief Minister of Bihar
mcqs.question: Who became the first BJP Chief Minister of Bihar after being sworn in at Patna?
options: Samrat Choudhary
Nitish Kumar
Syed Ata Hasnain
J.P. Nadda
mcqs.explanation: Samrat Choudhary was sworn in as Bihar Chief Minister at Patna and became the first BJP Chief Minister of Bihar. His appointment followed Nitish Kumar’s resignation after being elected to the Rajya Sabha.
